risks.risk: Item mismatch: seller description refers to a “double plate” hardware/console, but the photo shows only a PS4 game case.
risks.proof: Ask for photos of the exact item being sold: front/back of the console (if any), model label/serial sticker, and a photo showing the “double plate” part.
risks.if_unproven: Price as a PS4 game case only (worst case: no disc / not tested), until the actual item is confirmed.

risks.risk: Disc condition / whether the game is included and playable (if it’s actually the game being sold).
risks.proof: Ask for a photo of the disc (if present) and a short video showing the PS4 reading the disc / game launching.
risks.if_unproven: Price as not guaranteed playable (worst case: disc missing or untested).

risks.risk: If the seller is actually selling hardware, ports/overheating/repair history cannot be verified from the current photo.
risks.proof: Ask for a video test: all ports (USB, HDMI, audio) working + brief gameplay/boot time without shutdown.
risks.if_unproven: Price as hardware with unknown condition (worst case: not working/needs repair).

risks.risk: Receipt/pads authenticity and inclusion (UK receipt, original pads) not shown.
risks.proof: Ask for clear photos of the receipt and the pads included in the same frame as the item.
risks.if_unproven: Price without assuming receipt/pads are included.

proof_requests: Confirm what exactly is for sale: PS4 game only or a PS4 console/“double plate” hardware. Send 3–5 clear photos of the actual item.
If it’s the game: photo of the disc (front/back) and a short video of it launching on a PS4.
If it’s hardware: photo of the console model/serial label and a video showing ports working and no overheating/shutdown.
response.reason: The photo clearly shows a PS4 game case (Red Dead Redemption 2), but the seller’s claims describe different hardware details (“double plate”, ports, overheating, pads, UK receipt) that are not visible or verifiable from the single image. Missing decisive proof prevents a safe worst-case price.
